topic: Someone finds their grandmother's engagement ring in a pawn shop
text: Well, now, ain't that somethin'? Old Martha's ring, found in a place like that. It was always supposed to stay in the family, passed down with the blessings of the saints. I remember the tales, how it was as dear to her heart as the soil to a farmer's hands. To think it ended up in a pawn shop, among strangers, without a whisper of its history. Must've been tough times for one of the kin, harder'n the stony earth of a late spring. I reckon it's a call for us to tighten our bonds, maybe gather the harvest a bit closer, seeing as the world can scatter us thinner than a drought-struck field.
